A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5.4 report original LLM evaluations and regret-loss training experiments. The appendices include prompt ablations, training ablations, and empirical checks of theoretical results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations of two open-source LLMs and a 50-round horizon study in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The regret-loss objectives, single-layer and multi-layer models, and decision-making procedures are retained. Adding pretrained models to the evaluation does not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the represented random-loss environments: common uniform bounds and Gaussian mean 5 become randomized action-specific intervals and mean vectors. The other online-learning, bandit, repeated-game, and adversarial scenarios are retained. The renamed noisy-alternating counterexample is the existing less-predictable sequence.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 add Mixtral-8x7b-instruct and Llama-3-70B-instruct alongside GPT-4, GPT-3.5 Turbo, FTRL, and FTPL. This substantially extends the evaluated model comparisons beyond the GPT family. The repeated-game and regret-loss model comparisons retain their existing comparators.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly revises uniform/Gaussian loss sampling. Appendix B.2 adds a separate 50-round full-information evaluation alongside the retained 25-round tests. The feedback construction and regret metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that all downstream experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 and Figure 14 test whether the observed behavior persists over 50 rounds for GPT-3.5 Turbo, Mixtral, and Llama across four loss scenarios. This adds a focused horizon sensitivity study. Existing prompt and regret-loss hyperparameter ablations are retained.

E5.justification: A new Section 3.2 footnote identifies the plotted error bars as variability across generated environment instances, rather than LLM stochasticity. Error bars already existed in v1. The hypothesis-testing procedures and stated repetition counts are retained.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 contain new model results and revised GPT curves; Figure 14 adds 50-round results. For example, GPT-4's Gaussian full-information fitted exponent changes from 0.44 to 0.63 under revised sampling, preventing a same-setting performance interpretation. Figure 8 also changes some statistics, including the adaptive-case QR dynamic-regret trend p-value from 0.15 to 0.08. Table 1 and the regret-loss model results are retained.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, regret definitions, theorems, and appendix proofs are retained. Appendix A.3 adds an action-level expression explaining FTPL, equivalent to the existing policy formulation, without changing the mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same claims about empirical no-regret behavior, counterexamples, the hypothetical pretraining explanation, and regret-loss guarantees. The additional evaluations support those existing claims.

C2.justification: The quantal-response interpretation, explanations of failures, and limitations of the pretraining assumptions are retained. The new behavioral-summary paragraph in Section 3.2 repeats reasoning already present in v1 Section 4.2 and Appendix B.4.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds LLM Engine as an API used for experiments and identifies the additional instruction-tuned model variants. The training architectures, optimizer settings, learning rates, epochs, and batch sizes documented in Appendix D.8 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang et al. (2024) on transformers learning temporal-difference methods to related work, plus the LLM Engine resource citation. The main positioning relative to prior online-learning, game-theoretic, and in-context-learning research is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and heading revisions, updated author information, and terminology changes from calibrated agent to generalized QR and from less predictable to noisy alternating. Appendix B gains the horizon subsection, while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 gain additional curves, expanded legends, and revised axis ranges. V2 adds Figure 14, relabels Figures 7–8, and relocates or renumbers several retained figures. The overall visual format and Table 1 structure are preserved.

improvement.justification: The open-source comparisons and 50-round ablation broaden support for the empirical claims, while the error-bar clarification improves transparency. These gains outweigh a localized reporting problem: Section 5.4 still says it uses Section 3.2's loss vectors, but Figure 9 retains v1's results despite the revised generators. That unresolved connection limits reproducibility and the overall improvement.
